slot.brief: A source moving between two observers (approach and recede) or observer moving both ways; set up Doppler ratios and find source speed from ratio of the two apparent frequencies.

stem: In still air, a source moves toward stationary observer Q while observer P, behind the source, moves in the same direction at speed $\dfrac{c}{5}$, where $c$ is the speed of sound. The source recedes from P and approaches Q. If the ratio of the frequencies heard at Q and P is $25:18$, find the source speed as a fraction of $c$.

verdicts.working: Let the source speed be \(uc\). Then \(f_Q=f\,c/(c-uc)\) and \(f_P=f(c+c/5)/(c+uc)\). Hence \(\frac{f_Q}{f_P}=\frac{5(1+u)}{6(1-u)}=\frac{25}{18}\), which gives \(u=1/4\).

working:
$f_Q=f_0\dfrac{c}{c-u}$; $f_P=f_0\dfrac{c+c/5}{c+u}$; $\dfrac{f_Q}{f_P}=\dfrac{1+u/c}{(1-u/c)(6/5)}=\dfrac{25}{18}$; hence $u/c=\dfrac{1}{4}$.

Independent check: Let the source speed be \(uc\). Then \(f_Q=f\,c/(c-uc)\) and \(f_P=f(c+c/5)/(c+uc)\). Hence \(\frac{f_Q}{f_P}=\frac{5(1+u)}{6(1-u)}=\frac{25}{18}\), which gives \(u=1/4\).
solution:
For a moving source and moving observer, $f_Q=f_0\dfrac{c}{c-u}$ and $f_P=f_0\dfrac{c+c/5}{c+u}$.
Let $x=u/c$. Then
$$\frac{f_Q}{f_P}=\frac{5(1+x)}{6(1-x)}=\frac{25}{18},$$
which gives $x=\dfrac14$. Thus the source speed is $\dfrac{c}{4}$.
